title: Present perfect: have done
goal: Talk about experiences and recent news with have/has + past participle
intro: The present perfect (have/has + past participle) connects the past to now. Use it for life experience (“I’ve been to Japan”), for news and recent results (“I’ve lost my keys”), and with ever, never, already, yet and just. The time is not stated, or it isn’t finished.

rules.rule: A past action with a result now.
examples: She’s broken her phone. (It’s broken now.)

rules.rule: with just, already, yet, ever, never.
examples: Have you finished yet? I haven’t started yet.

mistakes.why: A finished time (yesterday) needs the past simple.

mistakes.wrong: Did you ever go to Kerala?
mistakes.right: Have you ever been to Kerala?
mistakes.why: For life experience, use the present perfect.

ex.y: Experience, no time given: have seen.

ex.q: I’ve ___ finished. Give me one minute.
Have you replied to the email ___?
I have met her last Monday.

ex.a: Have you ever tried South Indian coffee?

ex.q: Correct this: “I have seen that movie yesterday.”
ex.y: Yesterday is finished, so use saw.

talk: Tell the coach about places you’ve been, foods you’ve tried, and something you’ve never done but want to. Then say one thing you did last month, in the past simple.
